name: Blue Sapphire
spiritual: Opens the throat and third eye
physical: Traditionally associated with a calm, clear mind
Crystal healers link it to restful sleep
Many people keep it nearby for eye-strain comfort as a symbol of clear vision
summary: Blue Sapphire is the classic deep-blue corundum, a gem of royalty and truth, honored in crystal lore for wisdom, loyalty, focus and serene communication.
intro: Blue sapphire is the gem most people picture when they hear the word sapphire: a transparent corundum in shades from pale sky to deep royal and midnight blue. Its color comes from traces of iron and titanium in aluminum oxide. Only diamond is harder among natural gems, which means a sapphire can last for generations without losing its polish. The most prized stones show a velvety, intense blue with lively brilliance, from Kashmir, Myanmar and Sri Lanka, while Madagascar, Australia, Thailand and Montana supply many others. Most sapphires are heat treated to improve color and clarity, an accepted practice, and fine untreated stones command a significant premium.
history: Sapphire has been prized since ancient times. The name comes from Latin sapphirus and Greek sappheiros, likely referring originally to lapis lazuli before being applied to blue corundum. Medieval Europeans believed it protected its wearer from envy and kept the heart faithful, and clergy wore it as a symbol of heaven. In Persian lore, the sky was blue because it reflected the sapphire on which the earth rested. Sapphires have adorned royalty, including the engagement ring famously worn by Diana, Princess of Wales, now worn by Catherine. The stone is also a classic gift for fifth and forty-fifth wedding anniversaries.
meaning: Blue sapphire is a stone of wisdom, truth and loyal devotion. Practitioners link it to the throat and third eye centers, using it to support clear thinking, honest communication and calm focus. Its deep color is associated with the night sky and still water, symbolizing serenity and depth. People turn to it for study, important decisions or conversations where integrity matters, and to strengthen commitment and faithfulness in relationships. In Vedic astrology, blue sapphire, or neelam, is linked to Saturn and is considered a powerful stone best worn with guidance from an experienced astrologer. In crystal healing circles, it is seen as a stone of mental discipline and spiritual insight that encourages living by your truth.
howToUse: Wear blue sapphire as a ring, pendant or earrings for focus, calm and gentle authority during meetings and exams. Hold a stone between your hands in meditation, resting it at the brow or throat and breathing slowly. Place a small piece on your desk to encourage clear thinking when writing or studying. Gift sapphire jewelry as a symbol of faithfulness. In a grid, pair it with lapis lazuli, clear quartz and amethyst for wisdom and intuition work. Keep a smaller stone in your pocket before important conversations.
care: With a hardness of 9, sapphire resists scratches and can be cleaned with lukewarm water, mild soap and a soft brush. It tolerates sun, moonlight, smoke and sound for cleansing. Fracture-filled or diffusion-treated stones should avoid ultrasonic and steam cleaners and harsh chemicals. Dry with a soft cloth and store separately in a pouch, since sapphire can scratch softer gems. Although tough, it can still chip if struck hard on an edge, so remove rings during heavy work.
identify: Genuine blue sapphire has vitreous brilliance, a strong blue color that may show slight color zoning and natural inclusions such as silk or fingerprints under magnification. Lab-created sapphires are common and chemically identical but display curved growth lines or tiny round bubbles. Glass, synthetic spinel and dyed quartz are cheaper imitations. Most natural sapphires are heated, and some are beryllium diffused or glass-filled. Disclosure and a gemological report matter, especially for valuable stones.

faq.q: What is blue sapphire good for?
faq.a: In crystal tradition, blue sapphire is used for wisdom, truthful speech, loyalty and calm focus. It is a classic stone for study, meditation and commitment, and it suits those who want clarity and poise.

faq.q: Can blue sapphire go in water?
faq.a: Yes, it is very hard and can be washed in lukewarm water with mild soap. If a stone is fracture-filled, avoid soaking and harsh cleaners, and dry it carefully.
